headline: Canton house fire injures resident, kills dog and sends firefighter to hospital
dek: The Hickory Lane home was destroyed after a Sunday blaze and a Monday-morning rekindle; officials said the cause remained under investigation and the fire was not believed to be suspicious.
body: A house fire in Canton injured the home’s sole occupant, killed a pet dog and destroyed the residence before the fire rekindled hours later, sending a firefighter to a hospital for precautionary treatment. The first blaze began around 3:45 p.m. Sunday at 11 Hickory Lane, according to the [Canton Fire Department’s account reported by The Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/05/metro/canton-fire-destroys-home-hospitalizes-occupant-and-firefighter/).

Firefighters arrived to find heavy flames moving from an enclosed rear porch into the roof and attic of the two-story home. The crews initially tried to fight the fire from inside, but moved to a defensive exterior operation after the roof began to sag and partially collapse. Canton Fire Chief Jamie Meier said the fire was already well developed when crews arrived, The Globe reported. The structure was ultimately considered a total loss.

The resident was found injured outside the house and taken to a Boston-area hospital. Officials said the injuries were burns that were not believed to be life-threatening. A labradoodle was found dead inside the home. [NBC Boston](https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/canton-massachusetts-fire-injures-resident/4025904/) reported that the resident was expected to be OK, while the fire department said the property itself could not be saved.

Firefighters also faced a water-supply problem involving a nearby hydrant that was not working properly, according to the accounts. That detail matters because crews were dealing with a fire that had already reached the upper portions of the building and a roof that was becoming unsafe for interior operations. The reporting does not say how long the hydrant problem lasted or whether it changed the final damage assessment.

The danger continued after the initial fire was knocked down. The home had been boarded up when firefighters were called back at about 3 a.m. Monday, Oct. 5, after the fire rekindled. [WCVB](https://www.wcvb.com/article/firefighter-hospitalized-after-fire-rekindles-at-canton-home-where-resident-suffered-burns/74024607) reported that the rear of the house was gone and the front was unstable, leaving crews to work from outside while smoke and flames moved through the structure.

During the second response, a firefighter who became short of breath was taken to Milton Hospital as a precaution. A camper with a fiberglass shell and propane tanks at the back of the property also caught fire, and the heat melted vinyl siding on a neighboring home, according to The Globe. No additional injuries were reported in the accounts reviewed for this story.

The cause had not been finalized. The [Boston 25 report](https://cmg-cmg-tv-10020-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/news/local/crews-return-canton-home-after-fire-rekindles-overnight/WQ4QIWS6R5G4LAL6VDUJ2P2MHM/) on the rekindle said investigators were still working to determine what started the original fire, and the station described the Monday return as an ongoing investigation. The Globe reported that officials did not believe the fire was suspicious and that investigators considered embers from a portable fire pit on the back porch a possible origin. Those statements describe a preliminary assessment, not a final cause determination.

For Canton residents, the incident is a reminder that a fire can remain dangerous after visible flames are knocked down, particularly when a roof or attic has been compromised. The immediate consequences in this case include a displaced resident, a destroyed home, damage to a neighboring property and a firefighter injury. The available reports do not identify the resident or provide a detailed medical update, and they do not say whether the state investigation has reached a final conclusion.

The next step is the completion of the fire investigation by Canton officials and the Massachusetts State Fire Marshal’s Office. Until that work is finished, the confirmed facts are the injuries, the pet death, the total loss of the home, the overnight rekindle and the precautionary hospitalization of the firefighter; the precise ignition source remains unresolved.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Canton house fire injures resident and firefighter
